tasks.short: Collect legal and retention requirements, inventory where content sits, write the policy text, discuss it with legal, security and business owners, and update it after comments.

steps.what: Document management specialist collects legal, retention and security requirements
Document management specialist inventories which systems hold which content
Document management specialist writes the document management policy text

loop.input: The specialist's list of decided policy points and the library of legal and retention rules.
loop.output: Draft policy sections in the house format.
loop.check: Every rule reference must match an entry in the rule library, or it is dropped; points come only from the specialist's list; the specialist edits every section.
loop.stop: One draft per section; if rejected, the specialist writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template gives the headings, not the wording of each rule.

steps.what: Document management specialist assists in determining policies with legal, security and business owners
Document management specialist updates the policy after comments

tasks.design: A rule library with retention periods, legal bases and security rules ({DOCS}), kept with legal, replaces searching laws and old memos each time. Storage reports from the document system show content per site, age and owner, so the inventory is not built by asking around. A bounded step drafts policy sections from the specialist's decided points; rule references not in the library are dropped and the specialist edits every section. Comments are made in the shared document. Discussing the policy with owners stays with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were searched each time and the inventory built by asking around.
tasks.enabler_now: Document systems report content per site; language models draft text checked against a rule library.
tasks.still_hard: Departments keep content outside the document system.
tasks.human_edge: Finding a policy that legal accepts and users will follow.
tasks.altitude: The specialist edits policy text instead of writing it from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether drafts cite the right rules.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft policy text whose rule references can be checked against a library.
Personal data may be kept only as long as needed, so retention rules must be set per document type.

assumptions: Boundary: from the policy review to the policy updated; approval by management is outside.
Input contract: rule library kept with legal; fallback is searching.
Policy decisions stay with the owners.
research_questions: How much of each drafted section is kept?

already_counted.description: Document management specialist edits drafted sections.

incremental.description: Document management specialist keeps the rule library current with legal.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a new policy area; high: a periodic review of existing policies.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyse existing folders and document types, interview users, draft the taxonomy, test it with users, check it, and load it into the term store.

steps.what: Document management specialist analyses existing folders and document types
Document management specialist interviews users about how they search
Document management specialist assists in developing classification taxonomies by drafting terms in a spreadsheet

loop.input: Document titles, folder names and term counts from the content analysis.
loop.output: Candidate terms and a proposed hierarchy, each term with example documents.
loop.check: Every term must list example documents it covers; the specialist decides every term and its place.
loop.stop: One proposal per taxonomy branch; if rejected, the specialist drafts the branch.
loop.why_not_simpler: Counting folder names gives words, not a hierarchy.

steps.what: Document management specialist tests the taxonomy with users in sorting sessions
Document management specialist checks the final taxonomy
Document management specialist types the taxonomy into the term store

tasks.design: A content report from the document system ({DOCS}) lists document types, folder names and term counts per site, so the specialist does not browse folders by hand. A bounded step proposes candidate terms and a hierarchy with example documents; the specialist decides every term. Once checked, the taxonomy is imported into the term store from the spreadsheet instead of typed in. Interviews and sorting sessions stay with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Folders were browsed by hand and terms typed into the term store.
tasks.enabler_now: Content reports list document types; language models propose terms with examples.
tasks.still_hard: Departments use the same word for different things.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing terms that users in every department understand.
tasks.altitude: The specialist decides terms instead of compiling them.

reach.learn: Whether search finds the right documents.

evidence.claim: SharePoint autofill columns use a prompt to fill metadata per document, possibly wrongly, Microsoft warns.
Language models can propose candidate terms with example documents for a person to decide.

assumptions: Boundary: from the taxonomy needed to the taxonomy loaded; tagging documents is outside.
Input contract: content report available from the document system; fallback is browsing.
Users' time in sessions does not change.
research_questions: Do users find documents faster with the new taxonomy?

already_counted.description: Document management specialist reviews proposed terms.

incremental.description: Document management specialist keeps the term import file current.

approvals.approved_version: The taxonomy as checked by the specialist in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small taxonomy for one department; high: a large organisation-wide taxonomy.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather requirements with business and IT, set up department libraries and metadata, test them, migrate documents, and write user instructions.

steps.what: Document management specialist gathers requirements with business and IT specialists
Document management specialist implements document processing and retrieval by setting up department libraries and metadata by hand
Document management specialist tests the library set-up and permissions
Document management specialist migrates documents into the new libraries
Document management specialist writes user instructions

tasks.design: Site templates with standard libraries and metadata ({DOCS}) cover the standard department set-ups, about 70%, so these are applied instead of configured by hand; special set-ups are still built by hand. Test scripts check libraries and permissions after each set-up. Workflow and access profile configuration is a separate task. A migration tool moves documents with mapping rules from old folders to new metadata. User instructions start from a standard guide per template. Agreeing requirements stays with the specialist and IT.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each site was configured, tested and migrated by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Document systems support site templates, scripted tests and migration tools.
tasks.still_hard: Old folders with mixed content migrate poorly.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a department to give up its own folder habits.

evidence.claim: Document systems support site templates, scripted tests and migration tools with mapping rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the implementation planned to instructions written; user training is outside.
Input contract: site templates kept by the platform team; fallback is manual configuration.
Scenario: about 70% of departments fit a standard site template.
IT specialists' time does not change.
research_questions: Do set-up errors found after go-live fall?

incremental.description: Document management specialist maintains site templates and test scripts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many special set-ups; high: mostly standard departments.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read documents to judge type and sensitivity, enter metadata, decide security levels for sensitive documents, and log classification decisions.

steps.what: Document management specialist identifies documents by reading them to judge type, function and sensitivity

loop.input: Each document's text, title and location.
loop.output: Proposed document type, function and security level with a confidence.
loop.check: Proposals below the confidence threshold or at the highest security level go to the specialist; the specialist checks one in ten accepted proposals.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules on file names and folders misclassify most documents.

steps.what: Document management specialist classifies documents by entering metadata fields by hand
Document management specialist decides security levels for sensitive documents
Document management specialist logs classification decisions in a spreadsheet for audit

tasks.design: A bounded step in the document system ({DOCS}) proposes document type, function and security level with a confidence and fills the metadata fields; about 70% of proposals pass the threshold, while low-confidence and highest-level documents go to the specialist, who also checks one in ten accepted ones. Classification changes are kept in the system's version history, so no audit spreadsheet is kept. Deciding security levels for sensitive documents stays with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every document was opened, read and tagged by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Document systems can fill metadata columns from a prompt for review.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong proposals look plausible and can open sensitive files.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising that an ordinary-looking memo holds sensitive personal data.
tasks.altitude: The specialist reviews proposals instead of tagging every document.

evidence.claim: SharePoint autofill columns use a prompt to fill metadata per document, possibly wrongly, Microsoft warns.
Documents with special category personal data need restricted access under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from documents to classify to decisions logged; access management is outside.
Input contract: confidence threshold set by the specialist; fallback is manual tagging.
Scenario: about 70% of proposals pass the threshold; the rest are classified by hand.
The highest security level is always set by a person.
research_questions: What share of sampled accepted proposals is wrong?

already_counted.description: Document management specialist checks a sample of accepted proposals.

incremental.description: Document management specialist tunes the threshold and prompt.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half the proposals fall below the threshold; high: mostly routine document types.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The document management specialist keeps agreeing policies, deciding terms and security levels and working with IT; searched rules, browsed folders, hand configuration and hand tagging shrink.
skills_to_grow: Setting confidence thresholds and sampling proposals
role.ambitious_version: A specialist with more time on information governance.
